title: Profile release gates & ongoing maintenance for Redwood-verified model performance
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: As we onboard open models into the Redwood catalog we must publish Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) tied to a pinned model version and the hardware used. Objective: define the publishing workflow, release gates, metadata surface, and a maintenance cadence so customers can rely on published numbers for routing and cost planning. Scope: canonical benchmark harness, profile tiers (baseline/optimized/quantized), model version pinning policy, Console display and API surface, release & deprecation flow, automated re-benchmark cadence, and alerting when published profiles degrade. Out of scope: re-training models or changing model weights; platform-wide pricing changes unrelated to per-model measurements.
updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff with Runtime, Infra, and Console. Agreed canonical benchmark harness: bench/rt-bench shallow and long-form suites covering p50/p95 latency and steady-state throughput.

2026-03-06: Defined profile tiers: baseline (default FP16 settings), optimized (tuned batching + kernel flags), quantized (int8/4 where supported). Each tier must include costs estimation macro derived from token/time measurements.
2026-03-08: PM reviewed draft PRD; requested explicit rollback/deprecation policy and a ‘verified date’ field in profiles. Action: eng to define deprecation TTL and notification channels.

2026-03-11: Engineering proposed nightly re-benchmark for pinned versions with 3-run averaging to smooth GPU variance. Concern: benchmark noise on preemptible hardware; solution: restrict verification runs to dedicated test fleet and annotate profiles with hardware SKU.

2026-03-13: Console/Design walk-through. Design requested hardware and model-commit metadata visible on profile cards and a small explainer tooltip for customers describing how cost numbers are estimated.
2026-03-13: Added dependency on ENG-4001 (bench infra: stable runner) and ENG-4012 (profile publisher API).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A reproducible benchmark pipeline exists that consumes a model binary (versioned), runs canonical suites, and produces a standardized JSON perf profile containing p50/p95 latency, token/sec throughput, cost-estimate per 1k tokens, hardware SKU, model git/manifest reference, and verification timestamp.

AC2: Publishing workflow supports gating: manual review flag + automated checks (variance thresholds, throughput floor). Changes to published profiles require approver or a clear auto-publish rule documented in PRD.

AC3: Console shows verified profiles for pinned model versions including tier, hardware, verified date, and cost estimate; customers can view historical snapshots and subscribe to profile deprecation alerts.
AC4: API endpoint /models/{model}/profiles returns the same verified metadata as Console and supports region/hardware filters.
AC5: Automated nightly re-benchmark runs for pinned models are scheduled; when a nightly run deviates from published profile beyond threshold, an incident entry is created and PM + oncall notified.
AC6: Documentation and playbook exist for maintainers: how to add a new model, how to pin a version, how to retire a profile, and how to respond to profile regressions.
AC7: Security review completed if profile publishing requires access to customer-restricted infra (security_review_required=false unless changed).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: GPU variance produces noisy benchmarks. Mitigation: use dedicated verification fleet, run multiple seeds and report averaged metrics + stdev.
Risk: Cost estimates may be misinterpreted by customers. Mitigation: include a clear methodology doc and tooltip in Console; surface assumptions (batch sizes, padding, pricing tier).
Risk: Published profiles become stale as infra changes. Mitigation: automated re-bench cadence and deprecation TTL with email/console notifications before removal.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Build bench pipeline and publish profiles to a staging bucket; Console shows staging badges. Target: 2 internal models.
Phase 2 (limited beta): Enable publishing for select public models and invite 5 early customers to validate numbers for routing decisions.
Phase 3 (general availability): Publish verified profiles for catalog models, expose API endpoints, and include profiles in model selection documentation.
Fallback: If pipeline fails or produces high-variance results, revert to 'unverified' badge and surface fail reason in Console.
roles_and_responsibilities: PM: define acceptance criteria, coordinate cross-functional reviews, customer-facing messaging.
Runtime Eng: implement canonical benchmark harness and sampling strategy.
Infra Eng: provide dedicated verification fleet and stable runners (ENG-4001).
Console/Design: display verified metadata, history, and alerts UX.
SRE/Oncall: own alerting and runbook for profile regressions.
notes: We should avoid publishing platform pricing changes as part of these profiles; profiles are performance+cost estimates based on current public pricing formulas. Coordinate with Pricing before GA.
